title: Three cursor-local primitive searches
brief: Press S on the canvas to search only the canonical primitive library in a compact surface beside the pointer, choose with the keyboard, and insert without opening the command palette.
defaultWhy: Cursor Stack is the provisional implementation choice at 96/100. It is the only direction that keeps the Fusion-style pointer anchor, exposes enough labeled matches to disambiguate primitives, and makes ArrowDown + Enter obvious without growing into a command modal.
decisionHinge: The recommendation depends on labeled discovery mattering more than absolute minimum footprint. Moving about 17 weight points from Primitive discovery fidelity to Compact canvas continuity flips the recommendation to One-Line Rail; that would be appropriate if the catalog becomes familiar enough that users rarely need to compare matches.
invariants: Plain S opens beside the latest canvas pointer only when normal canvas shortcuts are eligible.
Results come from the existing SHAPE_LIBRARY_ITEMS catalog; commands and board text never enter the result set.
The same pointer, query 'arrow', and three matching primitives are used in every direction.
Ctrl/Cmd+P, Ctrl/Cmd+K, and Ctrl/Cmd+F retain the existing large command/find modal.
boundary: The gallery runs the open → filter → choose state machines with realistic SystemSketch content. Pointer capture, tldraw insertion, undo, focus restoration, viewport collision, and production hotkey guards remain simulated here and are verified only in the implemented app.

requirements.name: Pointer-local speed
requirements.why: The Fusion-inspired advantage is avoiding a trip to global chrome: the search should appear where attention and the intended insertion already are.
requirements.passCondition: From a canvas pointer position, the user can open search and reach a likely primitive without moving their gaze to a distant modal.

anchors.1: Search opens away from the working point or needs pointer travel before typing.
anchors.3: Search is near the work but adds a detour or unstable placement.
anchors.5: One unmodified key opens a stable, immediately focused search beside the pointer.

requirements.name: Primitive discovery fidelity
requirements.why: A small surface still has to distinguish similar catalog entries such as straight, curved, and elbow arrows without leaking unrelated commands into the list.
requirements.passCondition: The filtered result set shows only canonical library primitives and provides enough name/category/icon context to choose the intended one.

anchors.1: Results mix in commands or conceal which primitive will be inserted.
anchors.3: Results are scoped correctly but comparison or naming is weak.
anchors.5: Multiple similar primitive matches are compact, clearly labeled, and easy to compare.

requirements.name: Compact canvas continuity
requirements.why: The new surface exists specifically to avoid the current large modal and should preserve the spatial context of the function being edited.
requirements.passCondition: The search remains visually subordinate to the board, occupies only the space its current results need, and stays inside the viewport.

anchors.1: The surface reads as another modal or obscures most of the working context.
anchors.3: The board remains recognizable, but the surface is larger than its task requires.
anchors.5: Only a small cursor-adjacent region is covered and the intended insertion context stays legible.

requirements.name: Confident keyboard placement
requirements.why: The interaction should stay in the keyboard flow that plain S starts while making the insertion target and selected result unambiguous.
requirements.passCondition: Typing filters, keyboard navigation visibly moves one active result, Enter inserts it at the invocation point, and Escape cancels.

anchors.1: Selection or insertion location is ambiguous and the keyboard path is incomplete.
anchors.3: Keyboard insertion works but requires learning hidden focus or navigation behavior.
anchors.5: Focus, active result, Enter, Escape, and the insertion point are all evident in the surface.

hardGates.name: Canonical primitive-only catalog
hardGates.why: A second catalog would drift, while command results would violate the requested scope.

hardGates.name: Canvas-safe S and separate command modal
hardGates.why: Typing in inputs or shape editors must remain typing, and existing Ctrl/Cmd command/find shortcuts must keep their established surface.

variants.name: Cursor Stack
variants.thesis: A Fusion-like search field grows downward into a short ranked list, keeping labels and keyboard selection directly under the pointer.
variants.bestWhen: People need to compare several similarly named primitives and want a familiar typeahead list with no pointer travel.
variants.losesWhen: The library becomes so familiar that showing more than one result at a time feels wasteful.

decisions.label: Primary model
decisions.value: A six-row maximum ranked list attached to the search field.

decisions.label: Position
decisions.value: The invocation point is the upper-left anchor; the stack flips or clamps at viewport edges.

decisions.label: Selection
decisions.value: ArrowUp/Down moves a strong active row; Enter inserts at the frozen invocation point.

proof: The live hero moves through hidden, filtered-list, and inserted states from either the walkthrough or direct controls.
The three arrow matches remain simultaneously comparable while the board and function card stay visible.

story.title: Search and insert without leaving the pointer

steps.label: Press S at the function
steps.caption: The pointer is already inside normalize(); S opens a focused field at that exact screen point.

steps.label: Type arrow
steps.caption: Only three canonical library primitives appear, with the best match visibly active.

steps.label: Press Enter
steps.caption: The active Straight arrow is inserted at the frozen invocation point and the compact surface disappears.

fr1.evidence: The field and result stack share the pointer anchor inside the function card; no global chrome enters the path.

fr2.evidence: All three arrow types remain visible together with icons, names, categories, and a singular active row.

fr3.evidence: The 292×190 stack preserves most of the board, though it covers more canvas than the one-result rail.

fr4.evidence: Focus, active row, ArrowUp/Down, Enter, Escape, and the orange insertion target are all explicitly represented.

g1.evidence: Every shown result maps to an existing arrow item in SHAPE_LIBRARY_ITEMS; no command appears.

g2.evidence: The concept labels plain S as canvas-only and leaves command/find shortcuts in their existing global modal.

variants.name: Icon Constellation
variants.thesis: A compact search field opens a two-dimensional icon grid around the pointer, favoring visual recognition over ranked reading.
variants.bestWhen: The catalog is visually distinctive and people remember the primitive's silhouette more readily than its exact name.
variants.losesWhen: Similar primitives need precise labels or the number of matches makes two-dimensional keyboard travel harder to predict.

decisions.label: Primary model
decisions.value: A visual tile grid that uses the pointer as a local origin rather than a list edge.

decisions.label: Position
decisions.value: The tile field fans horizontally where there is room, then folds at a viewport edge.

decisions.label: Selection
decisions.value: Arrow keys move spatially between tiles; labels remain secondary to silhouettes.

proof: The live hero reveals the same three arrow results as visual tiles and completes the same insertion state.
The wider footprint and two-dimensional navigation are visible rather than hidden in prose.

steps.label: Press S at the function
steps.caption: A local origin pulse marks where the visual picker will fan out.

steps.label: Type arrow
steps.caption: Three arrow silhouettes fill a two-column tile field; Straight arrow owns the blue focus ring.

steps.label: Press Enter
steps.caption: The selected tile inserts at the same frozen point and the constellation collapses.

fr1.evidence: The constellation opens around the pointer, but its width can place some results farther from the focal point.

fr2.evidence: Large silhouettes aid recognition, while a tile grid makes the three similar arrow labels less scannable than aligned rows.

fr3.evidence: The picker remains far smaller than the modal, though its 346px fan obscures more horizontal function context.

fr4.evidence: The active tile is clear, but two-dimensional arrow-key order and a partly empty final row add navigation ambiguity.

g1.evidence: The same three canonical arrow items are represented; no command or board text is present.

g2.evidence: The design assumes the same canvas-only S guard and does not replace the global command/find modal.

variants.name: One-Line Rail
variants.thesis: A single horizontal result rail shows only the current best match beside the field, minimizing occlusion and making cycling explicit.
variants.bestWhen: People mostly know what they want, type distinctive queries, and care more about keeping the function visible than comparing several matches.
variants.losesWhen: A broad query returns similar primitives and the unseen alternatives matter to the choice.

decisions.label: Primary model
decisions.value: One active result plus a 1-of-N counter rather than an exposed result set.

decisions.label: Position
decisions.value: A low, horizontal rail straddles the pointer and prefers the least occluding side.

decisions.label: Selection
decisions.value: Left/Right cycles matches; Enter inserts the only visible candidate.

proof: The live hero demonstrates the same open, query, and insertion states in the smallest rendered footprint.
The missing simultaneous comparison is honestly visible: only Straight arrow is rendered while the counter reports two hidden alternatives.

story.title: Insert from the smallest possible search

steps.label: Press S at the function
steps.caption: The function remains almost entirely visible because the search has no expanded result body.

steps.label: Type arrow
steps.caption: Only the best result appears; the 1 / 3 counter signals that Left/Right can cycle alternatives.

steps.label: Press Enter
steps.caption: Enter inserts the sole visible candidate at the pointer target and restores the full canvas.

fr1.evidence: The field and current result form one pointer-local row with no scanning or mouse travel.

fr2.evidence: The visible result is richly labeled, but two valid arrow alternatives are reduced to an abstract count and cannot be compared.

fr3.evidence: The 380×78 rail is the shallowest direction and preserves almost all vertical function context.

fr4.evidence: Enter is unambiguous and Left/Right cycling is named, though unseen candidates make navigation less confidently predictable.

g1.evidence: The rail indexes the same canonical three-item filtered set and never admits commands.

g2.evidence: It uses the same canvas-only S contract and leaves command/find shortcuts untouched.
